notes: Taken from the Board of Elections' 46-day election notice, which lists every contest and issue with the precincts that vote on it and gives the full ballot wording of each issue, checked against the Board's sample ballots for all 51 precinct splits. Where the two differ, the sample ballot's wording is used.

Candidates are listed alphabetically by last name, not in ballot order: Ohio rotates the order of names from precinct to precinct. Certified write-in candidates are not printed on the ballot and are not listed.

"Where you live" uses the state voter file: a district or school levy is shown for a city, village or township when any of its voters live in that district. Your exact ballot depends on your precinct.
The Board's ballots do not give local issue numbers.

issues.title: Charter amendment: prohibit the construction of data centers (new Section 8.07)
issues.text: Shall Article VIII of the Charter of the City of Urbana be amended to add Section 8.07, to read as follows? Article VIII, Section 8.07. Prohibition of a Data Center. (A) the construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) as used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) as used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing and dissemination of electronic data and information, including but not limited to the implementation of artificial intelligence, through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems, or virtual currency mining. (D) this Section shall not apply to data centers, as defined in this section, whose sole purpose is to serve as a dedicated facility that supports the computing needs of a single organization or enterprise not otherwise engaged in the business of management, storage, processing, and/or dissemination of electronic data and information and which is wholly owned by that enterprise, and which has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of less than seven-point-five (7.5) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (E) this Section is self-executing.
